paragraphs.source_en: Nothing is harder to understand than the human mind. As for my master's present state of mind, is he irritated, or merely in a frivolous humor? Or is he seeking some trace of consolation in the writings left by ancient philosophers? I cannot make it out at all. Is he sneering coldly at society, or does he wish to mingle with mankind? Is he losing his temper over trifles, or standing aloof beyond worldly things? I simply cannot fathom him. We cats are very simple in that respect. When we want to eat, we eat; when we want to sleep, we sleep; when we are angry, we are angry with all our might; when we cry, we cry as though the world were ending. And we cats never keep anything so useless as a diary. Because there is no need to keep one. Perhaps men with two faces, like my master, need to keep diaries so that in a dark room they may vent the true selves they cannot show society. As for our feline race, I think our going, staying, sitting, lying down, defecating and urinating are all our true diary; there is no need to take such trouble to preserve every aspect of our real selves, and if one has time to keep a diary, would it not be better simply to sleep on the veranda? My master went on writing:

units.source_zh: 而且，我们猫儿绝对不记日记这样毫无用处的东西。

paragraphs.source_en: Ate dinner at a certain restaurant in Kanda. I drank two or three cups of Masamune for the first time in a long while, and this morning my stomach is in splendid condition. It seems that for a man with a weak stomach, an evening drink is the best remedy. I absolutely will not take Taka-Diastase, no matter what anyone says. After all, what does not work simply does not work.

paragraphs.source_en: In his diary my master attacked the stomach powder with reckless fury. It was as though he were quarreling with himself. This morning's irritation seems still to be showing its tail in the diary. Perhaps this is precisely where the true nature of human diary-keeping lies.

paragraphs.source_en: The other day So-and-so said, "If you give up breakfast, your stomach trouble will improve." I tried going without breakfast for two or three days, but my belly merely growled and there was no effect at all. Someone else advised me by all means to give up pickles; according to him, the source of all stomach ailments lies in pickles. His reasoning was that once pickles were stopped, the very root of the stomach trouble would be cut off, and recovery would be certain. From then on I did not touch pickles for about a week, but as no particular sign of benefit appeared, I have recently begun eating them again. When I asked another acquaintance, he said, "The only treatment is abdominal massage. But ordinary massage will not do; it must be the old Minagawa-school method, and most stomach ailments can be cured at the root with one or two sessions. Yasui Sokken was also very fond of this massage technique. Even a hero like Sakamoto Ryoma is said to have often received this treatment." Persuaded by this, I promptly went to Kami-Negishi and had them massage me once. But they said I would not be cured unless they massaged my bones, and that unless the positions of my internal organs were once turned upside down, a radical cure would be difficult. Their manner of massaging was simply atrocious. Afterward my whole body went limp, and I felt as though I had contracted sleeping sickness. After that one experience, I was quite defeated and stopped going. Mr. A said I must on no account eat solid food, so I spent an entire day drinking only milk; then my intestines made a booming, sloshing sound as if there had been a flood, and I could not sleep all night. Mr. B said, "If you breathe with your diaphragm and exercise the internal organs, the stomach's function will naturally become sound; you should try it." I tried this method a little too, but for some reason my abdomen felt uneasy. At times, when it suddenly occurred to me, I would apply myself to it with single-minded concentration, but after five or six minutes I would forget it. If I tried hard to remember it, my mind was always on my diaphragm, and I could neither read books nor write essays. Seeing me in this state, the aesthete Meitei teased me: "You are a grown man, not someone about to go into labor; stop doing diaphragm exercises." So these days I have given them up. Mr. C said, "Perhaps you would be better if you ate more soba noodles." So I promptly alternated between hot soba in broth and cold soba, but this only gave me diarrhea and had not the slightest effect. For a year now, in order to cure my stomach trouble, I have tried every method I could devise, but all have been in vain. Only the three cups of Masamune I sipped with Kangetsu last night certainly seem to have worked. From now on I shall be sure to drink two or three cups every night!

paragraphs.source_zh: 前几天某某说：“如果不吃早饭胃病就会好。”我试着停吃了两三天早饭，结果只是腹中咕咕作响，毫无效果。某某劝我不再吃咸菜，据他说，一切胃病的病根都出自咸菜。只要不再吃咸菜，就可斩断胃病的老根，必然康复。从那时起，我有一个星期未沾过咸菜边，可也没见什么功效，因而最近又吃开了。问了一下某某，据他说：“唯一的疗法是按摩腹部。但普通的按摩法不灵，必须使用‘皆川派’的古法治疗，一般胃病只要搞上一两次，就可以根治。安井息轩也曾极为喜欢这种按摩术。就连坂本龙马那样的豪杰，也时常接受这种治疗。”经他这么一说，我立即去上根岸，让他们给我按摩了一次。但是他们说不按摩骨节不会痊愈，又说不把内脏的位置翻转颠倒过来，便很难根治等。那种按摩简直残酷极了。治疗后浑身瘫软，就像得了昏睡病一样。领教这一次以后，我再也不去了。A君说千万不可吃固体食物，于是我一整天只喝牛奶，这时肠里发出隆隆的响声，简直像闹了水灾似的，弄得我整夜无法入睡。B先生说：“用横膈膜呼吸，使内脏得到锻炼，胃的功能自然会健全起来，你不妨试试。”这个办法我也稍微试了试，不知为什么总觉得腹部不太舒服。有时我突然想起来，便专心致志地做，可过不了五六分钟就忘掉了。如果努力去记它，心中便总想着横膈膜，既读不成书，也无法写文章。美学家迷亭看到这个状况，调侃我说：“你一个男子汉，又不是要临产，做什么横膈膜运动，还是算了吧。”于是这些天我便停了下来。C先生说：“你多吃些荞麦面条可能会好些。”我就不断地轮换着吃打卤面和汤面，结果弄得我不断腹泻，却丝毫不见功效。这一年来，为了治胃病，想尽了办法，可一切均归徒劳。只是昨晚与寒月呷了三盅“正宗”，倒颇为管用。今后每晚一定要喝上两三盅！
